A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching central theory and experiments. Text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support comparison; relocated sections and renumbered figures can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original neural-network score-fitting and denoising experiments on linear configurations, circles, and nonuniformly spaced points, including Figures 2, 4, 5, and 9.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds results on two-dimensional spherical manifolds embedded in higher-dimensional spaces, reported in Section 6.3 and Appendix J.4.

M1.justification: The score-matching objective, regularization-based variational formulation, Smoothed PL-ESF, and denoising dynamics remain unchanged. The local-averaging identity explains the existing estimator; the three-layer network is an additional experimental configuration.

E1.justification: Beyond v2's linear configurations and circles, v3 evaluates intrinsically two-dimensional spherical patches embedded in R3 and R20, using gridded and randomly sampled latent training points. Section 6.3 substantially extends tested geometry beyond one-dimensional data manifolds.

E2.justification: Section 6.1 retains the exact ESF, Smoothed PL-ESF, and NN-learned SF comparison. The circle and nonuniform-point comparisons also retain their methods. The new manifold experiments introduce no additional comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: Fixed-time NN training changes from 6000 steps at learning rate 0.0002 in v2 Appendix I.1 to 80000 steps at 0.0003 in v3 Appendix J.1. Section 6.1's documented weight-decay coefficient changes from 3 to 2. New manifold protocols use 36 or 64 training points, two- or three-layer networks, and Adam at 0.001 without weight decay. These are reported setting changes, without establishing that retained figures were rerun.

E4.justification: Figures 12–14 add a limited qualitative robustness check across ambient dimensions 3 and 20 and two- versus three-layer networks on a 36-point latent grid. These probe persistence of interpolation across embedding dimension and network depth. Existing regularization and tangent-versus-normal analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-run replication counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. Generated-sample distributions and histograms are retained as visual evidence, rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New Figures 6 and 12–14 report generated samples interpolating between training points on spherical patches under several embedding, sampling, and network configurations. This adds substantial qualitative evidence beyond v2's line and circle results. Original plotted results are retained, although some associated training settings are revised; no same-setting performance improvement is established.

T1.justification: Appendix I.1 adds a local-window averaging definition and its identity with the existing Smoothed PL-ESF, Equations 89–90. Appendix H also restores the missing continuous-mixture weight, 1−a+−a−, in Equation 86's KL-divergence derivation. The principal propositions and their stated bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that score smoothing explains interpolation and avoidance of full memorization, connect regularized two-layer networks to the smoothed estimator, and report nonlinear examples without explicit regularization. The added manifold experiments support these retained claims rather than redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly interprets the Smoothed PL-ESF as local-window averaging, with smaller delta corresponding to a wider smoothing window, in Appendix I.1. v2 lacked this precise mechanism interpretation. The substantive limitations concerning simplified data, architecture, and incomplete implicit-regularization theory remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link, JAX and single-TPU-v3 execution information, previously unspecified hidden widths of 1024 and 512, and manifold construction and experimental configuration details in Appendix J.4. These substantially expand reproducibility information. The Figure 4 animation link present in v2 is removed.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a substantive comparison with Zhang and Pilanci (2025), plus discussion of Bonnaire et al. (2025), Ye et al. (2026), and Zhang et al. (2025, 2026). Buchanan et al. (2025) is removed. The established positioning relative to smoothing, manifold, and NN-regularization research remains; publication updates to existing references are not new works.

P1.justification: The abstract and introductory motivation are extensively recast. Related work moves from Section 7 to Appendix A with four explicit subsections, while the experimental narrative and appendix organization are reworked. This substantially changes document structure despite retaining most core technical content.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a different document-wide layout with changed typography, headings, running rules, and figure placement. It adds five figures: manifold results in Figures 6 and 12–14 and the projection illustration in Figure 11. All nine original graphics are retained, with appendix plots renumbered and regrouped.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens support beyond one-dimensional examples through the manifold experiments, makes the local-averaging connection explicit, corrects the KL derivation, and provides more reproducibility information. The central theory and existing evidence remain intact. The overall gain is limited because the new evidence is qualitative and Appendix J.4.2 leaves training epoch counts unspecified.
